title: TRIVORTEX: The Three-Body (and N-Body) Problem in the Vortex Model with the Chaplygin Topological Integral
description: TRIVORTEX is the working title of a research document by Isaev Iskhak Khamzatovich that studies the three-body (and N-body) problem through a vortex formulation with a Chaplygin topological integral C_Ch = r²(θ̇ − q·A_θ). The executable document builds an L×L Hofstadter Hamiltonian with N embedded vortices, constructs a Lagrange-type closed-form rotating solution (Theorem 3.1: r_k(t) = √C_Ch·(1 + ε·cos(ωt + 2πk/3)), θ_k(t) = ωt + 2πk/3, ω = (2π/T)·e^(C_Ch/π)), and couples it to spectral statistics (GUE/GOE/Poisson), quantum-topological observables (Berry phase, Chern numbers, TKNN conductance), chaos diagnostics and real astronomical presets (Sun–Earth–Moon, α Centauri, Pluto–Charon–Nix), with an interactive 15-mode menu and a seven-format report engine. An independent verification ladder re-derives the core claims from scratch and certifies: the exact 2π/3 equilateral choreography and periodicity of the closed form (V1), the rigid Lagrange rotation at ω = 3Γ/(2πa²) (V2), and the conservation of the vortex integrals H, P, Q, I (V3–V4); the endpoint drift of the Chaplygin combination is recorded as a window-dependent diagnostic. Formerly released as “AB-Cloud Vortex System for N-Body Problem”; the physics and the 22-section structure are unchanged.
